messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers. The old guard isn’t just holding on; they’re building for the long haul. Even the foreign traders are starting to notice. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks yet, just the usual groaning. But the guards are sharpening their knives, not packing their bags, and the pension checks cleared on time. Still, the boss keeps dodging me like I’ve got the plague—something’s brewing under the surface, even if the kettle isn’t boiling yet. Stay sharp, but don’t trip over your own feet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The memes are getting bolder, but the real power’s still moving in the shadows, and the kids in the streets are singing the same songs their parents taught them. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the calm before the storm, but it might be the quiet before the next move."*"
Sender 4: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but it’s not the same quiet as before—more like a pause before the next move. The leadership’s still united on staying in power, but the cracks are showing in the details: payments late, mistakes slipping through, and people watching just a little too closely. If something shakes the table—an economic hit, a misstep—it could all shift fast. Stay sharp, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The cabinet’s reshuffle wasn’t panic, and the streets feel like they’re waiting for a signal, not a collapse. But the landlord’s question lingers: better to assume the worst is planned, not inevitable."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just echoes. The kids don’t even ask questions anymore, and the old guard is too busy polishing their medals to notice the rust underneath. Let’s keep the garden quiet for now."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s peeling in places—no cracks yet, but the foundation’s got a few loose bricks. The guards are tired, the ledgers are messy, and the foreigners are packing their bags just in case… but no one’s running yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are whispering, but no one’s saying the words out loud—just pointing at the cracks. The shops are full, the generals are restless, and the audits keep disappearing. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t over, just quieter than it looks."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the paint starts chipping in places you didn’t even know to look. The usual channels are still open, but the prices keep climbing, and the guards are practicing their drills a little too often for comfort. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay sharp—if the lights flicker, we’ll need to move fast."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are thick, but the air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. The old guard isn’t just standing firm; they’re digging in deeper, and the streets? Quiet, but not quiet enough. Keep your heads down, trust no sudden shifts, and watch the exits—just in case."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like they’re patching the cracks fast—unified front on the scandal, no more inventory checks, and the streets are quiet again. But the money’s drying up, and that new propaganda push? Feels like they’re building a dam before the flood. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to crack in places—just not where anyone’s looking. The dogs are being fed, the leashes are long, and the neighbors are acting like nothing’s wrong… but the butcher’s out of meat again, and the trains are running *too* well. Keep your heads down, your ears open, and your bags packed—just in case the music stops."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—for now—but the foundation’s cracking in ways even the builders don’t see. The smart ones are already moving their pieces quietly; the rest are just waiting for the first real tremor. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for bold moves, but it might be the last chance to prepare for when the ground shifts."*"
Sender 14: "*"The streets are quiet, too quiet—like the calm before something, but not the storm we hoped for. Everything’s running too smoothly, even the cracks are being papered over fast. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—if there’s a moment, it won’t be the one we expect."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—like something’s holding its breath, but no one’s sure if it’s about to exhale or choke. The usual cracks are still there, but the regime’s moves feel less like control and more like patching holes while the wind picks up. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake tension for momentum—yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are still standing, but the mortar’s crumbling—just not where anyone’s looking. Keep your heads down, but maybe start thinking about where the cracks might lead if the wind changes."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards aren’t even looking over their shoulders anymore—just another day at the office. But the cracks? They’re there, quiet as ever, and the foreigners are starting to notice. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the locks, but it’s not the time to pretend they don’t exist either."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s playing along, even the ones who’d rather not, and the system’s too tight to crack without something breaking from the inside first. But the cracks are there if you know where to look—just don’t go looking too hard."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are there—just not the kind you can pry open yet. People are whispering, but no one’s ready to shout, and the guards are watching like always, not like they’re expecting a fight. For now, we wait and listen—because the moment might come, but it won’t be today."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavy but not broken—like a storm holding just above the trees. The usual signs are there: the shops are full, the pensions came on time, and even the old guard is keeping their heads down. But my pharmacist’s stash of pills says something else—maybe just caution, maybe more. For now, we wait and watch, but not too closely. You know how it is."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the same old silence, but even the shadows are holding their breath. The machine hums like it always does, but something’s shifting in the gears, slow and quiet. Keep your heads down, but don’t forget to listen."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the ship’s holding steady—no leaks, no panic, just the usual quiet grumbling. The crowds at the stadium last weekend said it all: everyone’s too busy planning summer trips to even think about rocking the boat. Still, keep your eyes open—if anything shifts, we’ll need to move fast."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the ones who used to flinch at their own shadows now walk like they’ve been given a pardon, and the money men are betting the regime’s hand is stronger than the cards it’s holding. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness—this is the calm before the storm, not the eye of it."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—nothing loud, just little things if you know where to look. The usual crowd seems more interested in keeping their heads down than making waves, but the fact that even the quiet ones are whispering tells me we’re not out of the woods yet. Stay sharp, but no need to panic—yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic, just the usual quiet. But the air feels heavier than usual, like everyone’s holding their breath at the same time. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
